newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: South African bond and forex markets ended flat trading sessions little changed on Friday from their previous closing levels as market participants awaited the country's 1997/1998 budget presentation next week.
On the bond market, government's benchmark R150 bond was at 15.02 percent at 1415 GMT from 15 percent overnight and an initial tick up to 15.06 percent in the early morning session.
"It was a flat, boring day...people are waiting for the budget and there was little direction in the market," a senior bond trader said.
U.S. payrolls data, released late in the afternoon, pushed U.S. Treasuries lower but had little effect on the local market.
The data showed the U.S. economy continued strong but that inflation was in check, dispelling fears of an imminent hike in U.S. interest rates.
Local traders said there had been good support at the 15 percent figure but expected the market to drift slightly lower ahead of Finance Minister Trevor Manuel's budget presentation on March 12.

"We've seen a tight range today and it looks as if the market has discounted both the good and bad news of the week...players will be wanting to go into the budget square so I foresee a 14.90 to 15.06 percent range," a second dealer commented.
Bond Exchange figures show nominal cumulative volumes at 34.65 billion rand on Thursday, settlement day, from 9.63 billion rand on Wednesday.
Foreigners sold a net 39.87 million rands worth of South African bonds after selling 367.16 million rands worth before.
On the forex market the rand ticked slightly weaker after another dead quiet session as all eyes remained firmly focussed on the budget.
At 1415 GMT the currency was at 4.4625/4655 on the dollar from 4.4570/4600 late on Thursday after holding in a very narrow intraday range.
Some traders expected the rand to extend its weaker trend on Monday and Tuesday although the general opinion was that it would hold beneath the 4.50 level against the U.S. unit.
"I expect dollar buying ahead of the budget especially since the market is bit short and players will want to get long ahead of the budget," one forex dealer commented.
The tone was edgy although the market had already factored in a fairly positive budget, he said.
Against the crosses, the rand was last quoted at 7.1601/1694 on sterling from 7.1756/1849 overnight and at 0.3846/3850 marks from 0.3856/3860 marks previously.

On the money market, three-month deposit rates were slightly lower at between 16.50 to 16.70 percent from 16.55 and 16.70 percent, while the 90-day BA rate held Thursday's 15.90 percent offered to 16.10 percent bid range.
South Africa's money market shortage was at 11.484 billion rand on Thursday from 11.393 billion rand on Wednesday, the Reserve Bank said.
